title: Renting a Car and Road Safety
objectives: Understand the process and requirements for renting a car in the United States
Read and interpret common road signs and traffic rules
Describe a road incident or accident clearly to police or an insurance agent
Use comparative structures to evaluate transportation options including driving, bus, and rideshare

reading_passage.title: Driving in America: What New Residents Should Know
reading_passage.text:
For newcomers who are used to driving in other countries, getting behind the wheel in the United States can be both familiar and surprising. The basic rules of the road — stop at red lights, yield to pedestrians, follow speed limits — are the same as in most countries. However, there are specific American customs and rules that often catch new drivers off guard.

One common difference is the 'right turn on red' rule. In most states, including Oregon, drivers are permitted to turn right at a red traffic light after coming to a complete stop, as long as the way is clear. This rule surprises many drivers from countries where any movement at a red light is forbidden. Another difference is the four-way stop, where vehicles at four different directions all stop completely, then proceed one at a time in the order they arrived.

Renting a car in the United States requires a valid driver's licence — ideally an International Driving Permit alongside your home country licence — as well as a major credit card and proof of insurance. Most rental companies require drivers to be at least 25 years old, though some will rent to drivers aged 21 and older for an additional fee.

Before driving in a new area, it is worth downloading an offline map in case GPS service is unavailable. It is also important to know what to do in an accident: stay calm, do not move the vehicles unless they are blocking traffic, and call 911 if anyone is injured. Exchange contact and insurance information with the other driver, and take photos of the damage before leaving the scene.
reading_passage.source: Adapted from the Oregon Driver Manual and a newcomer driving guide published by Catholic Charities of Oregon, 2023

glossary.meaning: to slow down or stop to allow another vehicle or pedestrian to go first
an intersection where all four roads have stop signs and vehicles must take turns
an official document that allows someone to drive in another country using their home country licence
a business that lends cars or other vehicles to customers for a fee
to give and receive the same type of information or item with another person

comprehension.question: What are two things you need to rent a car in the United States, according to the passage?
comprehension.answer: A valid driver's licence (ideally with an International Driving Permit) and a major credit card. Proof of insurance is also required.

comprehension.question: What does the author imply when they say new drivers are 'caught off guard' by American driving rules?
comprehension.answer: The author implies that even experienced drivers from other countries can be surprised or confused by rules specific to the US, because they are different from what those drivers are used to.

comprehension.question: What does the word 'yield' mean in the first paragraph?
comprehension.answer: To slow down or stop to allow another vehicle, cyclist, or pedestrian to go before you.

comprehension.question: Why does the author advise drivers to download an offline map?
comprehension.answer: Because GPS service may not be available in all areas — particularly in rural or less-connected regions — and having an offline map ensures you can still navigate even without internet access.

language_focus.title: Comparative Adjectives and Adverbs for Evaluating Options
language_focus.explanation: When comparing transportation options — driving versus taking the bus, renting a car versus using a rideshare — we use comparative forms. For short adjectives, add '-er' (cheaper, faster, safer). For adjectives with two or more syllables, use 'more/less' (more convenient, less expensive). Use 'than' to complete the comparison.

examples.sentence: Taking the MAX is cheaper than renting a car for a daily commute.
examples.note: 'Cheaper' is the comparative form of 'cheap' — add '-er' for short adjectives.

examples.sentence: Driving is more convenient than taking the bus when you have heavy shopping bags.
examples.note: 'More convenient' uses 'more' because 'convenient' has three syllables.

practice.sentence: Rewrite using a comparative: 'The bus is safe. The train is also safe, but more so.'
practice.answer: The train is safer than the bus.

practice.sentence: Complete the comparison: 'Rideshare apps are ___ expensive ___ renting a car for one day.'
practice.answer: Rideshare apps are less expensive than renting a car for one day.

practice.sentence: Which is correct? A) Driving is more faster than walking. B) Driving is faster than walking.
practice.answer: B) 'Faster' already has the '-er' comparative ending — you cannot add 'more' as well.

vocabulary_in_context.definition: To give way to another vehicle or person, allowing them to proceed first
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: The basic rules — stop at red lights, yield to pedestrians, follow speed limits — are the same as in most countries.

vocabulary_in_context.definition: To give and receive information with another person, each providing the same type of details
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: Exchange contact and insurance information with the other driver, and take photos of the damage before leaving the scene.

vocabulary_in_context.definition: To officially allow something to happen under specific conditions
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: In most states, drivers are permitted to turn right at a red traffic light after coming to a complete stop, as long as the way is clear.

speaking_task.context: You are discussing with a friend how to get to a job interview that is 25 kilometres away. You are comparing three options: taking the bus, using a rideshare app, and renting a car for the day.
speaking_task.prompt: Compare all three transportation options for this specific situation. Consider cost, convenience, reliability, and any risks. Use comparative structures in your response and give a clear recommendation at the end.
useful_language: Taking the bus is cheaper than..., but it might be less reliable if there are delays.
A rideshare is more convenient than the bus because...
Renting a car is the most flexible option, but it is also the most expensive.
speaking_task.model_answer: For a job interview, I think reliability is the most important factor. The bus is definitely cheaper than a rideshare, but it is less predictable — a delay could make me late. A rideshare is more convenient and faster than the bus, though it is more expensive. Renting a car would give me the most control, but it is the most costly option and parking near the interview location could be difficult. I would choose the rideshare — it is more reliable than the bus and less stressful than driving somewhere unfamiliar.

writing_workshop.model_text: I prefer taking the bus to work rather than driving, for several reasons. First, the bus is significantly cheaper than paying for gas and parking every day. It is also less stressful — I can read or rest while someone else handles the traffic. On the other hand, driving is faster when I have errands to run after work, because the bus route does not go directly to the grocery store. Overall, for my daily commute, the bus is the better option, but having a car is more practical at weekends.
writing_workshop.model_analysis: Notice how the writer gives both sides of the comparison fairly, uses comparative adjectives throughout (cheaper, less stressful, faster, more practical), and ends with a clear personal recommendation.
writing_workshop.task: Compare two ways of travelling that you use or have used. Explain the advantages and disadvantages of each using comparative structures, and conclude with your personal recommendation.
success_criteria: Use at least four comparative adjectives or adverbs (cheaper, more convenient, safer, etc.)
Present at least one advantage AND one disadvantage for each option
End with a clear recommendation supported by a reason

quiz.question: According to the passage, what must a driver do before turning right on red?
options: Signal for three seconds and then turn
Flash the headlights to warn other drivers
Come to a complete stop and ensure the way is clear
Wait for a green arrow signal
quiz.explanation: The passage states: 'drivers are permitted to turn right at a red traffic light after coming to a complete stop, as long as the way is clear.'

quiz.question: What is a four-way stop?
options: An intersection controlled by traffic lights only
An intersection where all four roads have stop signs and vehicles take turns
A roundabout with four exits
A pedestrian crossing with four lanes
quiz.explanation: The passage explains: 'the four-way stop, where vehicles at four different directions all stop completely, then proceed one at a time in the order they arrived.'

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses a comparative adjective?
options: Driving is more faster than taking the bus.
Driving is fastest than taking the bus.
Driving is faster than taking the bus.
Driving is the faster than taking the bus.
quiz.explanation: 'Faster than' is the correct comparative structure — no 'more' is needed because 'fast' is a short adjective that simply takes '-er.'

quiz.question: What should you do immediately after a road accident, according to the passage?
options: Drive to the nearest police station
Stay calm, avoid moving vehicles unless blocking traffic, and call 911 if anyone is injured
Exchange insurance details and drive away as quickly as possible
Call your rental car company before doing anything else
quiz.explanation: The passage advises: 'stay calm, do not move the vehicles unless they are blocking traffic, and call 911 if anyone is injured. Exchange contact and insurance information with the other driver, and take photos of the damage before leaving the scene.'

listening_exercises.transcript: Thank you for choosing City Car Rental. To rent a car, you need a valid driver's license and a credit card. The basic price is thirty-nine dollars a day. Insurance is extra — it costs fifteen dollars a day and covers damage to the car. Please return the car with a full tank of gas, or we will charge a refueling fee.
listening_exercises.question: What happens if you return the car without a full tank?
options: Nothing happens
You pay a refueling fee
You lose your license
The insurance covers it

listening_exercises.transcript: Road safety rules in the United States are strict. Everyone in the car must wear a seat belt, including passengers in the back seat. Children need special car seats until they are big enough for a regular seat belt. Never use your phone in your hand while driving — in many states it is against the law. And always stop completely at a red light before turning right.
listening_exercises.question: What must all passengers do?
options: Sit in the back seat
Wear a seat belt
Hold their phones
Use a car seat
